A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SARMAE and SAR-1M. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials are readable and matchable despite added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SARMAE classification, detection and segmentation results in Tables 2–4, together with component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds data-scale, denoising, alignment-loss, optical-teacher and efficiency results in the supplement.

M1.justification: The MAE SAR branch, four-noise SARE augmentation, frozen DINOv3 optical encoder, cosine SARC loss and alignment weight of 0.1 remain unchanged. New denoising, loss and teacher variants appear as experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same SAR-1M sources and downstream classification, horizontal/oriented detection and segmentation coverage. The reduced-data experiment changes pretraining sample quantity within existing coverage; no new benchmark or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Copernicus FM and CROMA on FUSAR-SHIP 40-shot and SAR-ACD 30%. Tables 8–10 additionally evaluate LEE/BM3D/FROST-generated reconstruction targets, Gaussian-only augmentation, contrastive alignment and an MAE optical teacher, substantially broadening the alternatives tested.

E3.justification: v2 adds a fixed-ViT-B pretraining-scale comparison labeled 300k/30% versus 1000k and parameter, FLOP and training-time measurements. The existing 300-epoch pretraining budget, downstream label settings and fine-tuning configurations remain unchanged; v1 Table 7 becomes v2 Table 12.

E4.justification: v1 primarily ablates dataset pretraining, SARE and SARC, supplemented by attention and reconstruction examples. v2 adds tests of reduced data scale, denoiser-generated targets, Gaussian-only corruption, contrastive alignment, optical teacher choice and efficiency/scaling in Tables 7–11, substantially expanding analysis of the design choices.

E5.justification: Both report classification accuracy averaged over three runs with different random seeds, in v1 Section 9.1 and v2 Section 12.1. No new variance estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Previously reported entries in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged. Added results include Copernicus FM/CROMA accuracies of 87.61/83.71 on FUSAR-SHIP 40-shot, reduced-data SARMAE-S scores of 88.27/93.76 on FUSAR 30%/SAR-ACD, and new denoiser, Gaussian, contrastive and teacher comparisons. Table 11 adds approximately 45/60-hour ViT-B/L training costs. Several reference rows reuse existing results.

T1.justification: The speckle model, reconstruction and alignment objectives, and augmentation formulas in Equations 1–12 are mathematically unchanged. The added appendix rationale introduces no new formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of a first million-scale SAR dataset with paired optical imagery, the SARE/SARC contributions, and state-of-the-art classification, detection and segmentation performance. The added evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: New appendix explanations attribute denoiser underperformance to distorted semantic structures and contrastive-loss weakness to unreliable SAR negatives. They explain the frozen teacher and low alignment weight, while Section 11 interprets ViT-L's smaller-dataset behavior as overfitting. These extend the existing mechanism account and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses hash-based deduplication against downstream test sets, exclusion of optical images with at least 20% cloud cover, and training costs. Its abstract supplies a SARMAE project link and states that code, data and models are available, replacing v1's future-release promise. These disclosures do not establish that the underlying preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Copernicus FM, Any2Any, CrossEarth, TiMo and RoMA, plus restoration and pansharpening work, while retaining the main research-gap narrative. CROMA was already cited in v1; its new role is an evaluated comparator.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. v2 makes local wording and typo edits, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments and short appendix sections on SARC, DINOv3 and scaling. Existing fine-tuning, visualization and datasheet sections are renumbered 12–14.

P2.justification: v2 adds five appendix tables, expands Table 2, and compresses formerly full-width Tables 4–5 into single-column displays. Multiple figures and tables are repositioned throughout the main text and supplement. Figures 1–12 retain their content, but the overall table presentation and layout change substantially, including smaller text in key result tables.

improvement.justification: The new foundation-model comparisons and targeted noise, alignment and teacher ablations provide better support for existing design choices. Deduplication/filtering disclosures and the project link improve transparency. These gains are qualified by incomplete documentation of the denoiser experiment's label setting, Table 7's unreconciled 1000k versus 1.3M dataset counts, and reduced readability of Tables 4–5.
